judgments.reasoning_cat1: The preamble is internally awkward: EGL is labelled "(“EGL” or the “Guarantor” as the case may be)" although only one entity is being named, and the Borrower is made a party to an instrument granted "in favor of" the Facility Agent, leaving its capacity unclear. The nested description of Initial Lender / Subsequent Project Lenders "from time to time which shall become parties" is also loosely worded as to who counts as a Lender.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The cover page says the Agreement is "made by ESSAR GLOBAL LIMITED" alone, and Article III(o) speaks of "either Guarantor" and "either Guarantee Agreement" and "the Parent", suggesting a companion guarantee not identified here. The Borrower's party status also sits uneasily with SECTION 4.15's third-party beneficiary bar and with 2.01(a)(ii), which requires payment to the Borrower.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, conventional recital that the Lenders severally agreed to extend credit on the Credit Agreement's terms; no term in it carries competing meanings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with the consideration clause and with Article II's guarantee of the Borrower Obligations; nothing in the operative text contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One-line factual recital of affiliation; "affiliated group of companies" is loose but nothing operative turns on the boundary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing in Articles II–IV depends on group membership, so no conflict with any operative provision arises.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "substantial direct and indirect benefit" is a conclusory consideration recital whose content is not measurable, but it is standard and no operative right hangs on it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is a recital that could be set against the operative guarantee (a classic 2.3 pairing) if the Guarantor argued lack of consideration, but the NOW THEREFORE clause and Section 2.05's absolute-guarantee language point the same way.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional condition-precedent recital; "for the ratable benefit of the Lenders" is definite enough and is repeated in the operative consideration clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coheres with SECTION 2.01(a)(i), which measures the first guarantee period by satisfaction of the Credit Agreement's Article 4 conditions; no operative provision points the other way.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard operative-words clause; nothing in it is capable of two readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches the recitals and Article II; the only friction is that only EGL "agrees" here although the Borrower is a signatory party, which is minor.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "unless the context requires otherwise" is an open-textured escape hatch, and incorporation of undefined Credit Agreement terms means the meaning of this instrument depends on a document not before the reader.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Many operative terms — Commercial Operations Date, Project, Required Lenders, Total Commitments, Unrestricted Account, Parent, Disclosed Matters, Facility — are used in 2.01, 2.02 and Article III but defined only elsewhere, and "Parent"/"either Guarantor" in (o) may have no counterpart at all.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A self-referential definition with an amendment tail; there is nothing to construe in it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is used consistently throughout and does not clash with SECTION 1.03 or 4.14.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is a long chain of "all other obligations and liabilities" following enumerated specifics, which invites a general-versus-specific argument about its outer reach, and the sentence is broken by an intruding page header.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It defines Borrower Obligations by reference to "Obligations (as defined in the Credit Agreement)" while the local definition of "Obligations" (c014) points back to Borrower Obligations, a near-circularity that must be resolved by reading the two together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clause (ii) does not parse against the lead-in ("funds available to the Borrower required: ... (ii) any increase in the cost of the Project"), and "any actual shortfall, howsoever caused" plus "as determined by the Borrower or the Required Lenders" leaves both the trigger and the decision-maker genuinely uncertain, including whose determination governs if the two disagree.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The definition drives SECTION 2.01(a)(ii) and the whole of SECTION 2.02, and 2.02(a) requires a Lender's Engineering Consultant certification only for a Lender-initiated notice, so the amount owed can turn on which route was used.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The release trigger depends on offtake agreements "in form and substance and for a term ... reasonably acceptable" to two-thirds Lenders, and closes with a bare agreement to "negotiate in good faith" with no fallback — both classically contestable standards, in a single sentence of nearly 200 words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This date is the outer limit of the guarantee in both SECTION 2.01(a)(iii) and 2.01(d), so any uncertainty about when it occurs directly determines when EGL's liability ends; nothing else in the instrument supplies a mechanism if the Lenders withhold acceptance.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure cross-reference definition with no substantive content of its own.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The referenced Section 2.01(a) does define the term, but it bundles three structurally different obligations (guarantee, Deficiency funding, capped guarantee) under one label used throughout Articles II and IV.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "a material adverse effect on the business, financial condition, operations or performance or properties of the Guarantor since the date of this Agreement" is both vague in degree and oddly placed as to the temporal qualifier, which reads as attaching only to limb (a).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The term qualifies representations (a), (c), (d) and the notice covenant (m), so its boundary matters, but no other provision defines or contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A two-limb definitional shorthand; the drafting is elliptical (no verb) but the meaning is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with c009, "Obligations" is defined as "Borrower Obligations" which is itself defined by reference to the Credit Agreement's "Obligations", and SECTION 4.02(c) uses "the Obligations" without saying whose — a genuine, if small, loop.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb (e) expressly reverses ejusdem generis, directing that a general statement followed by specifics "shall not be limited to matters similar to the matters specifically mentioned" — an unusual instruction that itself becomes the battleground whenever a catch-all in the document is disputed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It bears directly on the reach of the catch-alls in c009 and in SECTION 2.05(iii), and cuts against the ordinary construction of the enumerated Deficiency limbs, but it is expressly stated and so mostly harmonises.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "for the purposes of and to the extent of the matters covered by this Agreement" is a self-limiting qualifier of uncertain scope: which matters are "covered" here is exactly what a conflict dispute would be about.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It grants this Guarantee priority over the Credit Agreement, yet SECTION 2.01(a) and 2.02(d) expressly subordinate their own mechanics to the Credit Agreement's terms and SECTION 4.08 treats the Loan Documents as one package — the priority rule and those deferrals must be reconciled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The three time-bounded limbs leave an apparent gap — a full guarantee only until the Article 4 conditions are satisfied, then Deficiency funding until the Commercial Operations Date, then a $250,000,000-capped guarantee — so whether the Borrower Obligations are guaranteed in the interval between closing and COD is genuinely arguable, and the cross-reference to "Sections 4.01 through 4.02 (including, in each case Section 4.04)" is internally odd.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: SECTION 2.01(d) says the guarantee "shall remain in full force and effect" until the earlier of the Release Date or payment in full, which does not sit comfortably with the period-by-period structure here, and the $250,000,000 cap must also be reconciled with 2.01(b)(ii)'s separate maximum-liability cap and 2.01(c).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb (i) is grammatically broken — "the obligations of the Guarantor hereunder are primary and notwithstanding the obligations of any other Person" — leaving the intended relationship to other guarantors and Collateral to be reconstructed by the court.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its cap by reference to fraudulent-conveyance law overlaps with the express $250,000,000 cap in 2.01(a)(iii) and with the solvency representation in Article III(e), and the two caps are not expressed to interact.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, clear statement that the guaranteed debt may exceed the Guarantor's capped liability; nothing lexically open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It presupposes and supports the caps in 2.01(a)(iii) and 2.01(b)(ii); it does not contradict them, though it depends on which cap applies.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The "earlier of" construction is definite on its face, though the trailing "notwithstanding that ... the Borrower may be free from any Borrower Obligations" pulls against the second limb's payment-in-full trigger.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read against 2.01(a), which already ends each guarantee limb at a different date, and against SECTION 2.06's reinstatement of a guarantee after it has terminated, this provision is difficult to harmonise — termination on the EGL Guarantee Release Date versus revival on rescinded payments.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The first sentence is ungrammatical — "shall notify the Guarantor ... to the extent a Deficiency at any time exists and that the Guarantor provides to the Borrower the amount" — so whether it imposes a mandatory notice duty and on whom the funding demand falls has to be reconstructed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Engineering Consultant certification is attached only to the Lender route, not the Borrower route, and 2.02(b) says the Lenders have no obligation to give notice at all, leaving the Guarantor's funding trigger under 2.01(a)(ii) dependent on a notice nobody must give.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear disclaimer of any duty to demand funds; the language is one-sided but definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against 2.02(a)'s "The Borrower shall notify" and against 2.01(a)(ii), which conditions the Deficiency obligation on the Guarantor receiving notice — so a court could be asked whether the obligation can ever arise absent notice.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "increase its charter capital" is an ill-fitting term for a Minnesota limited liability company, and the paragraph mixes a mandatory funding channel with a conditional "if the Guarantor decides", which blurs whether the Guarantor has an election.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: SECTION 2.02 runs (a), (b), (d), (f) — subsections (c) and (e) are missing — and the elective language here is hard to square with the unconditional undertaking in 2.01(a)(ii) to provide "the full and complete amount of any Deficiency".

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "to pay the cost or cost that has created the Deficiency" is repeated twice and is plainly a mechanical error, and the whole paragraph is again framed as "if the Guarantor decides".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: As with (d), the discretionary framing is in tension with the unconditional Deficiency undertaking in 2.01(a)(ii), and the missing subsections (c) and (e) leave the sequence incomplete.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long but conventional subrogation deferral; the drafting is clear, with the only softness being the reference to "any other Guarantor", who is never identified in this instrument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The deferral runs until "all Guarantor Obligations are paid in full ... and the Total Commitments are terminated", which does not track 2.01(d)'s alternative termination on the EGL Guarantee Release Date, and it defers to Section 6.07 of a Credit Agreement not reproduced here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A very long single sentence, but it is the standard catalogue of indulgences that do not discharge a guarantor; each item is concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It reinforces SECTION 2.05 and does not conflict with anything; the internal parenthetical "with the consent of such of the Borrower and the Guarantor as shall be required thereunder" is loose but harmonises.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It refers to "a Guaranteed Obligation", a term used nowhere else and never defined (the defined term is "Guarantor Obligations"), and limb (iii)'s "any other circumstance whatsoever" is an open catch-all following enumerated specifics.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: An "absolute and unconditional" guarantee of payment sits awkwardly with the express monetary cap in 2.01(a)(iii), the period limits in 2.01(a) and the fraudulent-conveyance cap in 2.01(b)(ii).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The reinstatement trigger is keyed to the insolvency "of the Guarantor" where such clauses normally turn on the primary obligor's insolvency, which is at least arguably a mechanical slip that narrows the clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Reinstatement of a terminated guarantee is hard to reconcile with 2.01(d), under which the guarantee ends outright on the EGL Guarantee Release Date, and with the caps in 2.01(a)(iii).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single short sentence; "guarantees that payments by it hereunder will be paid" is circular phrasing but the substance (no set-off, in Dollars) is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It says payments run "to the Lenders", whereas 2.01(a)(ii) and 2.02(d) require Deficiency funds to be provided to the Borrower as capital or a subordinated loan; and the no-set-off promise runs alongside SECTION 4.04's broad set-off right in the Lenders' favour.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The introduction is a plain repetition-of-representations clause; "each other date on which representations ... are made or deemed made under the Credit Agreement" imports an external repetition schedule but is not itself ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It announces that what follows are representations and warranties, yet paragraphs (h), (l), (m), (n) and (o) are express covenants and (o) imposes an obligation on the Borrower, so the Article's operative character does not match its lead-in.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard corporate-existence representation with a Material Adverse Effect qualifier on limb (iii); the wording is conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on the MAE definition (c013) and on "Governmental Authority" from the Credit Agreement, but nothing contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long but standard authority-and-enforceability representation with the usual bankruptcy and equitable-principles carve-outs; nothing lexically contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It represents that no consent or filing is required, which sits alongside (c)'s stamp-duty statement without conflict; the reference to "each other Loan Document to which it is a party" is broad but consistent with SECTION 4.08.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conventional no-conflict representation; the appended stamp-duty sentence ("except for those already paid") is a slightly awkward graft but its meaning is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with SECTION 4.02(b), under which the Guarantor indemnifies for stamp and other taxes, but the two are complementary rather than contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "would ... reasonably be expect to result" is an uncorrected grammatical error, though it does not really change the sense; "threatened" litigation is knowledge-qualified and standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It ties to the MAE definition and to the notice covenant in (m); no other provision points the other way.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard four-limb solvency representation; "unreasonably small capital" is a term of art from fraudulent-transfer law rather than a drafting defect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with 2.01(b)(ii)'s fraudulent-conveyance cap, and its limbs are relettered (a)–(d) inside a paragraph already lettered (e), which is untidy but not contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "shall at all time rank" is ungrammatical, it is a forward-looking covenant dressed as a representation, and "pari passu in right of payment in insolvency" narrows the usual formulation in a way that could be argued either way.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It appears in an Article introduced as representations and warranties (c030), and its restriction on ranking is not backed by any negative pledge elsewhere in the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "none of the or governors or managers of the Guarantor" is plainly garbled, and "a substantial Equity Interest" has no threshold, so its boundary cannot be applied.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It relies on "Disclosed Matters" and "Equity Interest", neither defined here, but nothing in the instrument contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The paragraph mixes a present representation, an express forward covenant ("this obligation shall be a covenant"), and an OFAC undertaking about "any part of the Facility" that the Guarantor does not itself draw, and "expeditious and effective steps" is an unmeasured standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its opening cross-reference "In addition to the requirements of Section 4.13" points to the Patriot Act clause, which imposes information duties rather than requirements of this kind, and its covenant character clashes with the Article III lead-in (c030).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Mid-sentence the clause switches subject — "to the extent that there may be attributed to the Borrower such an immunity" — in a representation that is otherwise entirely about the Guarantor, a mechanical error that changes whose immunity is waived.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The waiver supports SECTION 4.10's submission to jurisdiction, but the stray reference to the Borrower cannot be reconciled with the Guarantor-only framing of Article III.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single-line no-default representation; "Default in respect of the Guarantor" is terse but its sense is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "Default" is defined only in the Credit Agreement and is framed there around the Borrower, so applying it "in respect of the Guarantor" requires reading across instruments; (m)(1) uses the same phrase.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional information-materials representation with the standard projections carve-out; long but each element is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "Confidential Information Material" is defined only outside this instrument, but no provision here contradicts the representation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "substantially more favorable to the beneficiary thereof than as are provided by the Guarantor in this Agreement" requires a comparison across dissimilar guarantee terms with no benchmark, and the paragraph is a covenant sitting in a list of representations.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It distinguishes a "Project Lender which is not a Lender" — a distinction drawn from the Credit Agreement and from the preamble's "Subsequent Project Lenders" — and its covenant character conflicts with the Article III introduction (c030).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear five-Business-Day notice covenant; "any development or event that ... would reasonably be expected to" result in a MAE is a soft standard but a familiar and workable one.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is a covenant inside the representations Article (c030), and it permits notice to "the Lenders or the Facility Agent" while SECTION 4.12 routes notices through the Credit Agreement's addresses.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The closing proviso — that the restriction "shall not apply to an arms length sale or disposal of its assets or properties" — appears to swallow the prohibition entirely, since almost any disposal can be characterised as arm's length, leaving the covenant self-cancelling.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The covenant is the only asset-preservation protection in the instrument and underpins the solvency representation in (e) and the guarantee's value, so the proviso's reach must be measured against those provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It speaks of "either Guarantor", "either Guarantee Agreement" and "the Parent" — none defined or identified in this instrument, which has a single Guarantor — and the proviso permitting dividends and subordinated-loan payments largely qualifies the prohibition it follows.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It imposes the obligation on the Borrower inside an Article introduced as the Guarantor's representations and warranties (c030), and its "either Guarantor" language presupposes a companion guarantee that the preamble and cover page do not acknowledge.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The substantive no-waiver language is standard, but the parenthetical carve-out "(except by a written instrument pursuant to Section 4.12)" is definite on its face while pointing somewhere unexpected.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.12 in this Agreement is Notices, not amendments or waivers, so the only route by which a waiver can be effective is a cross-reference to a provision that does not provide for waivers — a specific internal misfit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "reasonable costs and expenses" and "reasonable fees and disbursements of counsel" are ordinary, judicially familiar standards; the clause is short and directed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It runs to the Facility Agent only while SECTION 4.02(b) covers the Facility Agent and the Lenders, a difference of scope but not a contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "any and all stamp, excise, sales or other taxes" is a catch-all following enumerated specifics, which leaves the reach of "other taxes" (income or withholding?) genuinely open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article III(c) represents that no stamp duty, registration charge or other statutory levy remains payable, which sits somewhat oddly with an indemnity against exactly those items; SECTION 1.02(e) also directs that catch-alls not be read down.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line survival clause; "this Section" is unambiguous in context (Section 4.02).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Survival past repayment of the Obligations must be read with 2.01(d), which terminates the guarantee on the earlier of the Release Date or payment in full, but survival of expense agreements is a familiar and reconcilable overlay.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear successors-and-assigns clause with a consent proviso; nothing in the wording is open to two readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: SECTION 4.15 covers the same ground but requires "the prior written consent of the Facility Agent and the Lenders", whereas this clause requires only the Facility Agent's consent — a direct inconsistency between two operative provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long but conventional bankers' set-off clause; every element (deposits, credits, indebtedness, claims) is specified and the trigger is a continuing Event of Default.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits alongside SECTION 2.07's promise that the Guarantor will pay "without set-off or counterclaim" — the two run in opposite directions but are addressed to different parties, and 4.04's closing sentence preserves other rights.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard counterparts clause; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The signature pages are executed in two separate sets, one bearing the Borrower's block, which the counterparts clause accommodates rather than contradicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard severability language, jurisdiction-limited and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with SECTION 2.01(b)(ii)'s statutory cap and 4.09's New York governing law without friction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard headings-for-convenience clause; nothing lexically open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: SECTION 1.02(f) permits references to sections and the table of contents titles Article III "Representations, Warranties and Covenants" though its lead-in speaks only of representations — this clause tells a court to disregard that heading.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional integration clause; "relative to subject matter hereof and thereof" is loose phrasing but its sense is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: SECTION 4.14 says "This Agreement constitutes the entire agreement" full stop, while this clause says the Agreement and the other Loan Documents together represent the parties' agreement — two integration clauses of different scope in the same instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence New York choice-of-law clause in capitals; there is nothing to construe in it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The document is "Executed as a Deed" by a Cayman company and enforcement is contemplated in Singapore under 4.10(a), which raises formality questions at the margin but does not contradict the governing-law choice.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause says proceedings "may be instituted in or (other than by the Guarantor) removed to" the New York courts while simultaneously waiving venue and forum non conveniens objections, so whether the forum is exclusive or merely permissive — the classic may/shall dispute — is left genuinely open, and the parenthetical restriction on removal is oddly placed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: SECTION 4.10(b) closes by preserving the Lenders' right to "commence proceedings against the Guarantor in any other venue where assets of the Guarantor may be found", and 4.10(a) contemplates enforcement in Singapore, so the New York submission cannot be exclusive against the Lenders while binding the Guarantor.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text contains an unresolved bracketed placeholder — "a new designee, appointee and agent with offices in [New York]" — and repeatedly mis-numbers the party ("Each of the Guarantor", "the Guarantor agree"), leaving the replacement-agent obligation imprecise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its final sentence preserving proceedings "in any other venue" pulls against the New York submission and venue waiver in 4.10(a), and "shall irrevocably designate" is future-tense although the designation is treated as already made.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The waiver itself is clear, but the inducement sentence refers to extensions of credit "TO THE COMPANY", a defined-party label used nowhere else in the instrument, where the borrowing party is "the Borrower".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "Company" appears in no other provision — the preamble defines EGL, Guarantor, Borrower, Lenders and Facility Agent only — so this term has no referent anywhere in the document.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The delivery methods are enumerated and "effective when received" is a definite rule; the only softness is that a permitted telefax requires a courier confirmation copy without saying which controls effectiveness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: SECTION 4.01 treats Section 4.12 as the provision authorising a waiver "by a written instrument", which this notices clause does not do, and it routes all Borrower, Lender and Facility Agent notices out to the Credit Agreement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The parenthetical "(for itself and not on behalf of any Lender)" is attached to a subject that already includes "Each Lender", which makes the qualifier incoherent as drafted, and "when appointed hereunder" has no appointment mechanism in this Agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article III(h) opens "In addition to the requirements of Section 4.13", treating this clause as imposing requirements on the Guarantor, whereas its operative first sentence is a notification by the Lenders.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "the entire agreement of each party" (rather than of the parties) is odd phrasing, but the merger effect is otherwise plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: SECTION 4.08 states that this Agreement and the other Loan Documents together represent the parties' agreement, while this clause confines the integration to this Agreement alone and supersedes everything else — the two clauses cannot both be given full effect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "the Guarantor shall not the right to assign or transfer" omits a verb, a mechanical error in the operative restriction itself, and the closing sentence denies rights to any Person "(other than the Lenders) not a party to this Agreement" although the Lenders are also not signatories.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It requires the consent of "the Facility Agent and the Lenders" whereas SECTION 4.03 requires only the Facility Agent's consent for the same restriction, and its third-party bar sits awkwardly with the preamble's inclusion of the Borrower as a party and with 2.01(a)(ii)'s obligation running to the Borrower.
